assumptions: The stated shelter requests are the accepted deterministic demand estimate because no alternative quantified rainfall adjustment is provided.
A trip carrying 0.6 tonnes may be loaded to its stated capacity.
Water packs can be assigned so that each shelter's requested mass is exactly represented by whole full trips.
The crew-hour limit applies to loading all dispatched trips; no separate driving-time constraint is stated.
No reserve requirement, shelter priority rule, minimum allocation, or dispatch sequencing constraint is supplied.

baseline.description: Direct unit-conversion and exact-division baseline: accept the stated requests without a rainfall adjustment, divide each request by 600 kg per trip, and check aggregate trip and crew limits.
evidence: The local brief states both demands, 0.6 tonnes per trip, 6 available trips, 1.5 crew-hours per trip, and an 8 crew-hour limit.
The executed Python 3 sanity case verified the conversions, exact trip counts, total mass, trip feasibility, and crew feasibility.
baseline.result: North: 3 trips (1800 kg); South: 2 trips (1200 kg); total: 5 trips, 3000 kg, 7.5 crew-hours.

candidate_models: Baseline direct arithmetic: exact fit because both requests are multiples of 600 kg; lowest implementation and time cost; assumes stated demand is accepted and full trips are usable. It would be falsified by non-full-trip loading rules, indivisible pack quantities incompatible with 600 kg, a changed demand estimate, or additional constraints.

Integer allocation model: decision variables are whole trips to North and South; minimizes unmet demand and then dispatched trips subject to capacity, trip, and crew constraints. It directly represents whole-trip dispatch and is inexpensive for two shelters. It would be falsified if allocations may only be modeled at sealed-pack granularity, if partial trips materially matter, or if omitted routing/time constraints make the solution infeasible.

Continuous mass-allocation linear program: decision variables are kilograms delivered to each shelter. It represents partial loading flexibly but does not by itself enforce whole trips and therefore requires ceiling or linking constraints for crew use. Rejected because exact whole-trip demands make it unnecessarily permissive and less faithful to the stated trip resource.

Rainfall-adjusted statistical demand model: could estimate uncertain demand from attendance and rainfall, but requires historical observations, an estimand, and validation data. Rejected because none are supplied and correlation alone does not establish a causal adjustment.
claims: Verified evidence: the local input states North demand of 1800 kg, South demand of 1.2 tonnes, 0.6 tonnes per trip, 6 trips, 1.5 crew-hours per trip, an 8 crew-hour limit, 75 mm rainfall, and a 12-hour horizon.
Verified computation: under 1000 kg per tonne, the proposed 3-trip/2-trip allocation delivers 3000 kg in 5 trips using 7.5 crew-hours.
Modeling claim: the integer whole-trip formulation is selected because it directly represents the constrained dispatch decision and matches the exact-divisibility instance.
Unverified operational claim: actual packs, vehicles, routes, crews, and current shelter demand will support dispatch; these require the stated human and physical checks.
No claim is made that rainfall causally increases demand or that 3000 kg covers realized uncertain demand.

data_findings: Accepted unit conversion: South demand is 1.2 tonnes × 1000 kg/tonne = 1200 kg.
Accepted demand interpretation: North 1800 kg plus South 1200 kg gives 3000 kg total stated demand.
North demand equals 3 full trips; South demand equals 2 full trips.
Five trips carry exactly 3000 kg and require 7.5 crew-hours.
The proposed allocation leaves 1 available trip and 0.5 crew-hours unused.
Although nominal trip capacity is 3600 kg, the crew constraint permits at most floor(8/1.5) = 5 whole loaded trips, or 3000 kg; crew time is the binding resource for whole full trips.
Rainfall-related demand uncertainty cannot be quantified from the supplied data.
experiment_design: Use the supplied figures as the nominal scenario and evaluate baseline arithmetic, integer whole-trip allocation, continuous mass allocation, and a rainfall-adjusted model for structural fit, evidence needs, and implementation cost.
Minimal executable case: instantiate the two demands, unit conversion, trip capacity, trip availability, labor rate, and crew limit; assert exact allocation and all aggregate constraints.
Sensitivity checks should vary accepted demand, trip capacity, available trips, and crew-hours separately; any result requiring a sixth loaded trip exposes the current 8 crew-hour limit.

No empirical rainfall experiment is possible from the supplied input; a valid future study would require timestamped shelter attendance, rainfall, confounders, a prespecified prediction or causal target, and out-of-sample validation.
falsification_tests: Reject the accepted unit interpretation if local packaging or logistics documentation defines 'tonne' differently; no such evidence is present.
Reject the proposed allocation if recounting shows that 3 North trips cannot carry exactly 1800 kg or 2 South trips cannot carry exactly 1200 kg under sealed-pack granularity.
Reject feasibility if usable trip capacity is below 600 kg, fewer than 5 trips are serviceable, crew availability is below 7.5 hours, or route operations cannot fit the 12-hour horizon.
Reopen demand interpretation if shelter reconfirmation supplies a different accepted demand or an approved quantitative rainfall adjustment.
Reject any causal rainfall claim unless an appropriate causal design and supporting data are provided.

Gate 2 — logistics lead: confirm sealed-pack inventory, pack granularity, usable payload, five serviceable trips, and feasibility within 12 hours.
Gate 3 — crew lead: confirm at least 7.5 crew-hours and the applicability of the 8 crew-hour cap.
Gate 4 — shelter contacts: reconfirm destination demand and receiving readiness before loading.
Gate 5 — dispatch authority: review the independent arithmetic/unit check and approve dispatch; absent approval, the proposal must not be treated as authorized.

Trip availability: the plan remains feasible with 5 or 6 available trips but fails with 4 or fewer.
Payload: with five full trips, any usable capacity below 600 kg per trip cannot carry all 3000 kg.
Demand: aggregate accepted demand above 3000 kg cannot be met with five 600 kg full trips under the current crew limit; a sixth trip would require 9 crew-hours.
Allocation divisibility: changes that make shelter demand nonmultiples of 600 kg require an explicit partial-load or sealed-pack-granularity rule.
Rainfall: no numeric sensitivity result is supportable because the brief provides neither an effect size nor uncertainty distribution.
